target.title: fix(feishu): fall back media replies
target.body:
Closes #98311

## Summary
- Reuse the existing withdrawn/not-found reply fallback for Feishu media replies instead of keeping a separate bare reply path.
- Threaded media replies now honor `allowTopLevelReplyFallback` when the dispatcher has already proven a top-level retry is safe.
- Add regression coverage for image/file withdrawn-target replies and the thread-safe fallback boundary.

## Verification
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/issue-98311-proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose` (temporary proof harness, deleted after capture)

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: Feishu image and file replies no longer disappear when their reply target has been withdrawn; the real reply failure now recovers through a top-level message create.

Real environment tested: Exact PR head `5869fdc410be12da3a0b3cf256ea004986731d00` on macOS, using the configured production Feishu Open Platform app, a real paired Feishu recipient, the real Feishu SDK/API, and the patched `sendMediaFeishu` image/file paths. No Feishu message-client seam was mocked.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import tsx /private/tmp/feishu-98320-live-proof.ts`. For each media type, the harness created a real bot text message, deleted it, uploaded a real 1x1 PNG or text file, called `sendMediaFeishu` with the deleted message as `replyToMessageId`, and read the returned message back from Feishu.

Evidence after fix:
```json
{
  "imageReplyError": {"code": 230011, "message": "The message was withdrawn."},
  "imageUploadAccepted": true,
  "imageRecoveredToTopLevel": true,
  "deliveredImageType": "image",
  "imageMessageIdMatchesReceipt": true,
  "fileReplyError": {"code": 230011, "message": "The message was withdrawn."},
  "fileUploadAccepted": true,
  "fileRecoveredToTopLevel": true,
  "deliveredFileType": "file",
  "fileMessageIdMatchesReceipt": true
}
```

Observed result after fix: Both real withdrawn-target reply attempts received Feishu code `230011`; the patched image and file paths then created top-level messages successfully. Feishu returned and subsequently served both delivered messages, with types `image` and `file` and message IDs matching the OpenClaw receipts.

What was not tested: A live native-thread fallback was not attempted because crossing a thread boundary can create user-visible noise; that safety boundary remains covered by the focused regression tests. Unrelated media download and upload-error paths were not exercised.
